Il m’a fallu du temps pour trouver un assez bon logiciel permettant de faire des listes de choses à faire mais même si Any.do est le meilleur que j’aie pu obtenir, j’ai aussi une déception : j’inscris les courses à faire et les démarches à effectuer au fur et à mesure que j’y pense, forcément pas dans l’ordre où elles doivent être accomplies.

Or je suis très déçue de constater que le logiciel ne les met pas automatiquement en ordre chronologique : si j’inscris une démarche à effectuer demain à 11h00 et qu’ensuite je pense à une course urgente à faire à 09h00, et puis après à quelque chose qui interviendra à 10h00, Any.do les laisse tels quels, dans l’ordre où ils ont été inscrits, 11h00, 09h00, 10h00, au lieu de les rétablir automatiquement dans leur ordre horaire.

Ce n’est pourtant pas sorcier de penser à une chose aussi simple...

body:
A great feature of the any.do app is the daily planner. It allows you to pick and choose the tasks to be done today. It really helps plan out the day. So loud they will wake up light sleepers in other rooms. Once you have started the daily planner you are stuck in it until all tasks are sorted with each task making a high picked sound. There is no being discreet with this app.
Hopefully this issue gets a fix like a volume button in the planner but otherwise this app gets full thumbs up for simplicity and effectiveness. title: Overhyped. Buggy. Limited Functionality.
body:
I really wanted to like this app. So much so that I committed to a year of premium service and switched wholesale from my other productivity tools.

Overall I've been really disappointed with the experience. The app is very buggy and seems very immature given how long the tool has been around. In particular syncing can be hit and miss. Sub tasks can't be reordered so anyone who likes organization and hierarchy will struggle. Setting due dates is laborious as is using location based reminders- unless you already have the address in your contacts. If you use the term 'call' when creating a to-do the app will link to a contact's phone number but often links to incorrect phone numbers belonging to alternate contacts. 

Any.do moment is a great feature but without a useful app behind it, I've found it quickly becomes gimmicky. Far easier just to set an alarm to prompt the planning of your day. 

So with 7 months of paid service I'm switching back to my previous free service as its more effective. 

Coles notes? A pretty app that places more emphasis on interface than actually getting things done. Save your money.

Things I love

- subtasks (although I would prefer it still show up as one task)
- beautiful clean interface
- ability to invite others to tasks

title: It's the user interface (and the categories or contexts)
body: I have been GTD'ing since ~ 2005, maybe even longer now that I think about it. title: Best to-do app out there
body:
This app is exactly what my little OCD brain was looking for in a to-do app. Quickly add items to one of several lists like personal, work, "someday" (LOVE that one!), etc. Tap to view whole item, tap the pencil icon to edit, and swipe to delete (which strikes and greys item out, throwing it to the bottom of the list for you). Delete it completely when ready. 
  Turn device to landscape and it ALSO shows your calendar in list mode, a feature that seemingly disappeared in Calendar's regular view mode for ios7! [side note: in calendar, you now have to hit the search icon to look at things in list mode]. What I love about this is, you can edit your calendar items in any.do and it syncs the update in your regular calendar!
  Wonderful layout and design, Customizable settings (including high-contrast), definitely worth downloading!

title: Beautiful, very useful app.
body:
I love this app! Visually, it's beautiful. The interface is clean, polished, and sleek. It's a pleasure to navigate through it.

In terms of functionality, it does almost everything you would want a task app to do. The "Any.Do Moment" feature is brilliant and helps you to keep on top of your day. 

But, what really puts this app over the top is the Chrome desktop app. If you use Gmail and Chrome, you can download the desktop app which syncs your computer and mobile device. It integrates so well that it basically turns your inbox into a personal assistant. With one click you can turn an email into a "to do" item or tell the app to remind you to take action on an email at a certain time. Very useful.

I just have a few minor quibbles, which I hope will be resolved through updates. First, it doesn't let you choose unique reminders like every Friday or every third Saturday of the month, etc. It would be helpful to have that because that would actually reflect how people do certain things in their life.

Second, it seems difficult to delete a task once you have created it. Maybe it's just me, but as far as I could see, the only way to delete a task is to mark it as "done" and then remove it. There should be a way just to delete it. 

Overall, great app. I have used a number of task apps, and this is by far my favourite.

title: Best to do app I've used
body:
The best feature of this to do app is being able to easily move tasks between the following categories:

Today
Tomorrow
This week 
Later

If you turn it over to landscape mode you are also able to drag a task to any other date in the month. This is great for splitting up your tasks into manageable chunks and also for planning your days and schedule accordingly. 

The shared task sync between other users does not seem to appear to work well or consistently, otherwise I'd give this app 5 stars. Also it occasionally does not shift the day forward.

Another great new feature is the option to plan your day on a regular basis each morning, confirming your set tasks for the day or deferring them to another time.

title: Honest Review: "Perfect"
body:
For its simplicity this application is efficient & very powerful. It is very smooth synchronizes perfectly between both my iPhone & iPad. 

The GPS allows you to set reminders when you arrive or exit a location, as well as the standard essential functions you would expect from a reminders app. 

While typing it will allow has the functionality of predictive-text, completing phrases while you insert them. 

You can sort your tasks by creating personal folders, or use the embedded mini-engine "AnyDo" which allows you to quick set tasks in sequences of "Today", "Tomorrow", "Someday", etc. In time you'll find this little jewel quite useful for quickly sorting items. You also have the ability to re-use deleted tasks. 

Overall, if you are searching for an app that is simple & powerful; it delivers!

title: Best in Class
body:
By far the best app of it's type, great interface that is quick and easy to use. 

Love how quickly you can add a new task (by voice); how you can easily mark something as important; and how easily you can put off a task until the next day/week/someday by simply dragging it down.

Unfortunately it's greatest strength is also it's weakness. The simplicity often comes at the cost of flexibility & advanced features. 

I don't like the Upcoming category. If I want to do a task sometime in the next week I'm forced to either place it in upcoming or I have to set a specific day & time.

Complaints aside, this app is awesome and easy to use. Most importantly it's effective at helping you get things done.

title: Keeping it simple for better or worse...
body:
First thing first, Any.Do sports a simple, intuitive (as long as you're used to iOS UI conventions) and responsive interface. While the cloud synchronization is quick and works as intended, this app stays fully functional without a network connection. 

There is a good balance between the number of features and keeping everything breezy, but some stuff is missing:

- Default parameters for new task.
- Being able to switch in landscape while creating a task (I have a hard time with the portrait keyboard).
- A way to assign a task to both a folder and a date while it is created.

Keep up the good work! Can't wait for the HTML5 version of the service!
